transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
Thousands of flights across the country are still delayed or cancelled following the FAA's
nationwide ground stop Friday.
Christopher Allum from member station KQED filed this report from San Francisco International
Airport.
A long line snakes around empty carousels at baggage claim.
Those were eager to share their frustrations.
This is the United States of America.
This shouldn't not be happening to these people.
We have teachers that need to get back to their students.
Everyone's bags were everywhere normal was checking.
Anyone could walk up to anyone's bag and there were like hundreds of bags downstairs.
Just exhausted, tired, a bit frustrated of course as well but the main thing is we get
home alright.
That was Sylvia Garcia, Lindsay Smith and Tim Fischl.
For NPR News, I'm Christopher Allum in San Francisco.
Microsoft says its products are back online after a days-long outage knocked out critical
services to companies and governments around the world.
NPR's Marissa J. Lange has the story.
Two days after a massive outage shut down Microsoft products like Outlook, Teams and
Co-Pilot, its AI assistant, the company announced all services had been restored to its more
than 430 million customers.
The outage affected international government operations, healthcare services, businesses,
banks, schools, courts and even the U.S. House of Representatives.
In a post on X Friday, the technology company said it was "deeply sorry" and described
the outage as a "technical issue."
It said Microsoft was not the victim of any cyber attacks or rogue AI agents but instead
blamed the failure on a network upgrade.
Marissa J. Lange, NPR News.
Down detectors said it received outage reports from over 70 countries.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Washington proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding
land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the proposal comes as Russia is ramping up its demands.
In comments reported by the AFP news agency, Zelensky said the U.S. had asked whether Ukraine
would withdraw from the eastern Donbass region if it is able to join NATO.
Zelensky said Ukraine is discussing "specific security guarantees" from NATO and the European
Union and that he would ask Ukrainians if they accepted the terms, if formally offered.
Meanwhile, Putin is maintaining his position that Ukraine hand over territory Russia does
not control, and he's rejected any foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine.
The Kremlin also renewed an old demand that NATO pull back military infrastructure from
central and eastern European countries that joined NATO following the breakup of the Soviet
Union.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
Ukraine has long sought to join NATO, but Russia continues to view that as a non-starter.
You're listening to NPR.
Bloomington, Indiana has passed a city ordinance banning what is being called "super intelligent
AI."
Ethan Sandweis, with member station WFIU, has the story.
The ordinance refers to "hypothetical artificial super intelligence," AI that exceeds human
capabilities and can improve itself.
Bloomington City Council member Dave Rollo says he's concerned about warnings by industry
leaders that it could become a threat to humanity.
AI experts disagree on where that threshold is, making the law difficult to enforce.
But Rollo says local enforcement is not the point.
He hopes it will put pressure on the federal government to act.
Imagine a quiltwork of hundreds of cities saying the same thing.
Now you're forcing the topic.
You're making lawmakers at higher levels take this seriously.
City Councilors removed parts of the ordinance that would allow the city to fine AI users.
For NPR News, I'm Ethan Sandweis in Bloomington, Indiana.
Fans celebrated the legacy of Rocky Balboa 50 years after the film Rocky with a record-breaking
gathering in Philadelphia.
Hundreds gathered yesterday at the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art to break a record
for the most number of people dressed as Rocky.
The city organized events this month to honor the fictional boxer, including a sprint up
the iconic stairs of the museum and the rededication of the Rocky statue.
The 1976 film was written by Sylvester Stallone.
It became a cultural phenomenon.
It also won the Oscar for Best Picture.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Thousands of flights delayed or cancelled after FAA's nationwide ground stop, with long baggage lines at San Francisco airport
Microsoft says Outlook, Teams and Copilot restored after days-long outage affecting customers worldwide
Zelensky says Washington proposed Ukraine cede land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership
Bloomington, Indiana passes city ordinance banning hypothetical super intelligent AI
Hundreds dress as Rocky Balboa at Philadelphia Museum of Art, setting record 50 years after the film
